rationale: A burst internal water supply line causing flooding damage to the policyholder's own basement structure and contents is classic covered property damage under homeowners insurance.
claim_summary: Sam Patel (POL-1004) returned from a work trip to find approximately 2 inches of standing water across the entire basement, caused by a burst supply line under the upstairs bathroom sink that ran for roughly two days. Damage includes buckled hardwood floor, water-soaked drywall (up to 1 foot height), and ruined stored contents. This is a high-severity claim requiring urgent mitigation and on-site assessment to prevent secondary damage such as mold.

case_facts.damage_description: hardwood floor buckled, drywall soaked up to 1 foot, stored boxes ruined
case_facts.cause: burst supply line under upstairs bathroom sink, ran for approximately two days

rationale: Wind damage to the policyholder's own roof structure (four shingles) with no third-party involvement or theft.
claim_summary: Wind damage to roof shingles above back porch during last weekend's storm; four shingles blown off with no water intrusion. Estimated repair cost $400. Claim falls below $2,500 deductible and will not result in payout.

case_facts.description: four shingles blown off by wind, no water intrusion
